summary: Well‑executed, preregistered paired confirmatory study of a generate–validate–repair (G‑V‑R) pipeline for LLM‑produced vendor CLI configurations. The run is reproducible and fully artifacted; under the declared model/prompt/validator every shared initial candidate passed the deterministic validator (baseline = 300/300), so the guarded single‑repair intervention was never exercised and the paired difference is 0.00 (McNemar two‑sided p=1.00, 95% CI [0.00,0.00]). The manuscript correctly reports this ceiling outcome and publishes hashes. The work is methodologically sound and reproducible but the paper omits a small number of clarifying, artifact‑resolvable items needed for completeness and interpretation.
critical_issues: Manuscript omits an explicit per‑vendor breakdown (task counts and paired contingency cells per vendor) despite repeatedly asserting a multi‑vendor manifest; this is evidence the reviewers must see to support the multi‑vendor claim.

Statistical reporting lacks an explicit methodological note for the degenerate contingency case (n10 = n01 = 0): how the chosen tests/CI behave in this situation and the implications for hypothesis interpretability (i.e., that the preregistered comparison was uninformative because there were zero discordant pairs).

The paper states exploratory repair diagnostics were pre‑specified but does not explicitly mark those diagnostics as uncomputed because no repairs were invoked; this should be a clear, unambiguous disclosure (artifact‑traceable) so readers do not expect repair‑success statistics.
required_revisions: Insert a compact per‑vendor results table (for Cisco IOS, JunOS, Arista) showing task counts and the 2×2 paired contingency (n11,n10,n01,n00) for each vendor; populate from execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution/scoring/*.json and cite the artifact hashes (e.g., execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = 6d99060659a722e6a91dd2abd7baca45a2aefb41e124b049124d5ea2632cb4b3).

Add a short statistical-methods paragraph (or a sentence in Methods/Results) that: (a) explains handling of the degenerate paired table when n10=n01=0, (b) states why exact McNemar and the bootstrap percentile CI produce p=1.00 and CI=[0,0] here, and (c) clarifies the consequence that the preregistered confirmatory test cannot demonstrate a positive repair effect when no initial failures occur. Use the existing analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl artifacts as evidence.

Explicitly state (in Results and Limitations) that the preregistered single‑repair policy was not exercised (repair call count = 0), that repair diagnostics are therefore vacuous for this run, and that any claims about repair effectiveness must be re‑framed as future‑work requiring non‑zero initial failure rates; cite the execution manifest model_calls_used and the scoring/repair trace artifacts (e.g., provider call and repair trace files hashed in the execution manifest).
optional_revisions: Add a brief per‑vendor difficulty summary (mean/median difficulty tags or required_command_count) drawn from the task_manifest entries to help readers assess manifest hardness.

Include an inline excerpt or appendix paragraph reproducing the exact vendor‑adapter prompt template used for initial generation (or point to the exact transformation_manifest entry and show the relevant prompt text) to improve immediate interpretability for readers who do not fetch artifacts.

Discuss briefly whether alternative repair budgets (iterative repairs) or a non‑shared initial candidate design would be more informative in future confirmatory tests; cross‑reference the preregistered exploratory questions (E1–E3).
